analysis:
Independently checked the supplied workflow, changelog, build-documentation patches and replayed surrounding source against the indexed threat model. .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml:19–37 adds an hourly/manual GitHub-hosted dispatcher with job-scoped actions:write and contents:read. It does not check out or execute dev source, interpolates repository/token values through quoted environment variables, and dispatches a fixed workflow on a fixed branch. API failures stop the script. No supported credential exposure, injection, release-authority escalation or provider-runtime regression was identified.
The changelog lines 3–4 and docs/developer/build.md additions at 340–356 describe the target branch's full-suite and failure-reporting contract; they do not modify authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or cache controls. T-041's isolation and storage mitigations are unaffected by the visible changes. The bounded run query at workflow lines 31–37 is non-atomic, so the documentation's no-overlap claim is stronger than the implementation; no evidence establishes a security-sensitive consequence of overlap.
Material unresolved integration contract: dev's .github/workflows/ci-dev.yml and its called workflows are not supplied. Review their workflow_dispatch handling, runner admission, cache writes, credential access and release/publication gates before concluding that automatic hourly execution preserves A-005/A-011/A-017 and T-054 protections. Missing implementations are not proof of a regression. Source replay is incomplete (two units omitted), so this conclusion covers only the visible evidence and does not clear the entire PR.
